frames.whyAnchor: The document/archival grammar done at 9: REAL archival material (19th-c lithograph figures) arranged with wit — the two men face each other so the hand-lettered OK becomes their conversation. One saturated field (orange), one accent (rough red swash), zero decorative noise. Texture is genuine print grain, not a CSS filter.

Document-collage hook: layered REAL artifacts (survey maps, declassified pages, stamps, redaction bars, flag) each with its own history, unified by typewriter type on red bars. Density with hierarchy — a dozen sources, one reading order.

frames.video: What If You Fall into a Black Hole?
frames.whyAnchor: A designed WORLD: accretion disk built from a dozen layered ring strokes (orange→magenta→white heat ramp), star field with three density tiers, custom character at story scale, and the annotation (red circle + arrow) treated as part of the composition, not stuck on top.

A literal in-video frame: the tree of life as a real diagram — ~50 species silhouettes, each readable at thumbnail size, connected by a routed white tree on one flat blue field. Information IS the art; nothing decorative anywhere.

frames.video: Why Sanctions Don't Work Against North Korea
frames.whyAnchor: The data-world grammar: map as environment (not clipart) — glowing subject shape, fine instrument-panel texture (coordinates, tick numbers, dashed boxes) that rewards a second look, and a strict two-level type hierarchy with a single accent color carrying meaning (pink = the subject).
